- Location advantage — proximity to railway station and bus station
- Natural demand balancing between national and inbound tourists due to the difference in their holiday periods
- Ability to extend the product portfolio by offering various types of facilities
- A team of able and experienced industry professionals, with regular employee-feedback and retention practices (monthly staff functions, religious programmes, picnic tours)
- Proper, strong, independent and adequate internal control systems supplemented by an extensive programme of internal audits
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical tension and ongoing wars depressing travel demand — Management states recent geopolitical tensions and ongoing wars, particularly in West Asia and surrounding regions, have created significant uncertainty for the global hospitality and tourism industry, with direct and indirect effects on travel demand, operational costs and overall business stability; wars reduce global tourist confidence through safety concerns, travel advisories and fear of instability.
- Cyber security threats and data breaches — Flagged as a significant and evolving risk for the hospitality industry: as digital adoption increases the attack surface continues to expand, making robust cyber security frameworks essential. A hotel holds guest personal and payment data, so a breach is both an operational and a reputational exposure.
- Competitive intensity in its city of operation — The MD&A lists 'Healthy Competition in the city' among the situations the Company must operate within, and the cautionary statement names competition first among the significant factors that make a difference to the Company's operations.
- Government policy, regulatory and tax-regime change — The cautionary statement names changes in Government policies and regulations and in tax regimes as significant factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. The Company's demand narrative also leans on government initiatives (Dekho Apna Desh, UDAN connectivity), so a policy reversal cuts both ways.
- Dependence on Indian macroeconomic conditions and discretionary travel spend — The cautionary statement names economic development within India as a significant factor, and the growth narrative rests on rising middle-class incomes and disposable income driving discretionary leisure travel — a demand base that contracts quickly in a downturn.
- Human-capital dependence and retention — The Company states it depends extensively on its human assets, considers them one of its most precious assets and 'not affordable to lose', with 137 employees in 2025-26; retention measures (regular employee feedback, monthly staff functions, religious programmes, picnic tours) are described as necessary to preserve competent employees.
- Need for green-technology investment and a change in how hotels do business — Management states green technology investments and a change in how hotels conduct their business 'will be necessary', and describes the industry as becoming sustainability-focused where organisations that invest in innovation, digital capabilities and environmental responsibility strengthen their competitive position — implying an obligatory spend to stay competitive.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: H S India Limited operates in the hospitality/hotel industry, serving domestic leisure travellers, inbound tourists and corporate houses in and around Surat. The Company positions its properties in the mid-market segment, offering comfort and facilities configured to guests' requirements, and states its locations benefit from proximity to a railway station and a bus station. The Company describes itself as extending its product portfolio by offering various types of facilities.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- Mid-market positioning, which management states faces very little disturbance versus other segments
- Location advantage — proximity to railway station and bus station
- Natural demand balancing between national and inbound tourists due to the difference in their holiday periods
- Ability to extend the product portfolio by offering various types of facilities
- A team of able and experienced industry professionals, with regular employee-feedback and retention practices (monthly staff functions, religious programmes, picnic tours)
- Proper, strong, independent and adequate internal control systems supplemented by an extensive programme of internal audits
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Target the mid-market hospitality segment at its locations, providing comfort and a look configured to guests' requirements, on the view that the mid-market faces very little disturbance
- Extend the product portfolio by offering various types of facilities
- Position properties to capture both business and leisure demand as hybrid work increases demand for hotels providing business facilities alongside leisure amenities
- Balance national (domestic) and inbound tourist demand, which management says can be easily managed because their holiday periods differ
- Reduce power consumption and overall energy cost — using PNG (Piped Natural Gas) in the kitchen and other operational areas, solar panels for water heating, power savers in electric panels and LED fittings in guest rooms
- Invest in human resources by providing various facilities, to strengthen presence in the existing business and take advantage of emerging growth opportunities in the hospitality sector
- Maintain strong internal control systems supplemented by an extensive programme of internal audits and documented policies, guidelines and procedures
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no capex or expansion project for the Company. Management's forward commentary is limited to industry-level growth (regional airport expansion under UDAN, improved road and high-speed rail connectivity opening Tier-II and Tier-III hospitality markets) and to its own positioning in the mid-market segment; no new property, room addition, refurbishment or project timeline is named. The Directors' Report states the Company has no Subsidiaries, Joint Ventures or Associate Companies, that no loans or guarantees under Section 186 were given during the year, and that there have been no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position between the year-end and the date of the report. The only asset-side investment described is energy-related: PNG in the kitchen and operational areas, solar panels for water heating, power savers in electric panels and LED fittings in guest rooms; technology absorption is stated as nil.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising incomes among India's growing middle class driving strong growth in domestic leisure travel, with the middle class described as a key driver of India's tourism growth
- Supportive government initiatives — improved connectivity and the Dekho Apna Desh campaign — making travel more accessible
- Expansion of regional airports under the UDAN scheme improving connectivity to Tier-II and Tier-III cities and enabling growth of new hospitality markets
- Improved road networks and high-speed rail connectivity reducing travel time and increasing tourist mobility
- Rise of hybrid work and 'bleisure' travel increasing demand for hotels that provide both business facilities and leisure amenities
- Continued expansion of the hotel sector in emerging nations as more people worldwide gain disposable income and travel more frequently, opening previously untouched markets
- Industry shift toward technology-driven, customer-centric and sustainability-focused operations, with green technology investment described as necessary
- Management view that long-term prospects for the travel and tourism industry in India are attractive and that Directors look forward to the future with confidence
- Headwind: geopolitical tensions and ongoing wars (particularly in West Asia and surrounding regions) creating uncertainty for global hospitality and tourism, reducing tourist confidence and affecting travel demand and operational costs
- Headwind: cyber security threats and data breaches as an evolving risk, with the attack surface expanding as digital adoption increases
- Local competitive context described as 'healthy competition in the city', with location advantage from proximity to railway and bus stations
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
